title: A backward org makes the linker hand out wrong label addresses, with nothing to notice it.
detail: Last-match scan over a table a backward org makes non-monotonic. Reproduced by derivation from the existing org_backward_overwrite test with a growing stub: correct 7, returns 5. Parcel out on branch parcel/shift-offset-org. Seats P2 and CACHE hit the same function for COST, not for this defect; that pair is recorded separately.

title: A bit test against a PC-relative label writes its address over the bit number, emitting a valid instruction that means something else.
detail: Both front-ends pass a hardcoded extension offset of 2; encode_bit emits the bit-number word first, so the correct offset is 4 (static) and 5 (indexed). The repo's own capstone_diff support module documents the asl witness 083A 0001 0002. Byte-neutral: aeon has no btst pcrel site. Parcel out on branch parcel/btst-pcrel-offset.

title: One language's align still writes padding bytes the other language stopped writing two days ago, and the test comparing them cannot see the difference.
detail: AS moved to reserve + asl_align_pad at 84c48a7b and touched only that side; .emp still emits Fill and rounds up unsigned where the shared rule is signed. The parity gate places data after the align in all three cases and flattens with 0x00, so fill and no-fill are identical. MUST land with the DAC bank recompute or the drum bank moves off its boundary silently.

title: The address-of-here builtin is baked before placement while labels follow placement, so the two disagree.
detail: The comment justifying same-section-only tracking says staleness hits labels and here() equally; that stopped being true at the placement rework. No here() test runs a placement pass. Exposure is data sections, not code, because a relaxable branch makes here() provisional and therefore correct.

title: A source file missing one closing keyword quietly loses a byte and reports success.
detail: find_block_end treats the file's last line as the missing closer. Reproduced against a real binary: AA 01 02 03 04 where AA 01 02 03 04 05 is correct, exit 0. Twelve lines away the code refuses a no-verdict if condition for precisely this reason. This is the class the AS-replacement project exists to eliminate.

title: A macro that calls itself twice never finishes, because only its depth is capped.
detail: Depth cap 64, breadth unbounded. The same file already argues the global-budget case for nested while and adds one; it was never carried to macros. Reached in practice via the unterminated-block defect, which can manufacture a recursive macro from source that never contained one.

title: A repeat block has no iteration limit at all, so a large count hangs the assembler with no diagnostic.
detail: while checks two caps; rept checks neither. Nested empty repeats reach ten billion body runs and time out silently.

title: One stray byte in a RAM-placed section makes the linker try to allocate the whole address space and die without a diagnostic.
detail: flatten sizes its output buffer from a placed ADDRESS rather than a size. Allocation failure aborts, so catch_unwind cannot turn it into an error. The correct guard, validate_section, exists and is not on the CLI path.

title: Two data directives silently truncate an out-of-range value where the third refuses it.
detail: dc.b range-checks and errors; dc.w and dc.l cast. The comment eight lines below the truncating line argues at length that truncating is the silent-wrong-bytes class.

title: Seven separate reviewers found the same mistake: something is checked in one place and then used somewhere that never sees the check.
detail: Sites: AS align (i64 guard, u32 consumer, panics in release); ds.b/w/l; .emp bank attribute; Z80 symbolic addresses on a truncating fixup where the emp twin range-checks; dc.w/dc.l; the abs.w window checked on three paths and not the eager fourth; comptime checked arithmetic against link-time wrapping. The correct idiom is already present at three sites, so these are drifts. Ruled to land as ONE parcel.

title: The lint guaranteeing every skipped check announces itself is blind to a wrapped line, and five live announcements are already through the hole.
detail: It only reads a format literal beginning on the same line as the macro. The five live sites say NOT MEASURED, which is in its own forbidden vocabulary, and are green only because of a line break. There is no rustfmt config and no fmt check, and five compliant sites already exceed the default width, so a routine reformat would shrink the census.

title: Four documents say the landing bar fails on a skipped check; the landing bar never reads the skip count.
detail: The exit decision reads CARGO_RC, FAILED, CLIPPY_RC and RECONCILED. The only real enforcer is the nightly lane, which is not the landing bar. A strict landing run carrying skip lines prints RESULT GREEN and exits 0.

title: The guard certifying that a byte-moving freeze was proved on an emulator only checks that the field is not empty.
detail: Five anchor-moving freezes satisfy it with an ab value that is the name of the preceding chain entry, chaining back to the bare string master.

title: Three port tests carry comments claiming a proof the code does not perform.
detail: The zero is the branch condition, not an assertion; one arm asserts a slice is empty when its own bounds make it empty by construction. A prior sweep hardened the comparison helper and missed the arm that skips the helper, so the hardened helper now makes the trio look covered.

title: A generated field the manifest calls dead is still stamped into hundreds of lines, and names test binaries that do not exist.
detail: repin.toml declares the tests field no longer read by anything while repin.rs still renders it. Three named binaries are absent from the tree, on the two most-read constants in pins.rs.

title: A number of pinned regions have no consumer anywhere in the code.
detail: ADJUDICATED: seat GATE reported 33 with an unstated predicate; seat B2b enumerated 22 with line numbers, a stated predicate and a control. The packet takes the enumerated set, on this lane's own rule to write the set and never the count. Spot-checked two plus the control.

title: The project's continuous integration has been failing for ten days, and the failing check is the one guaranteeing a bare run refuses.
detail: Last green 2026-08-27T11:18:17Z. The failing rows are bare_run_refuses.rs, and CI is the declared partial run whose refusal they exist to observe. Found on the hub's ask after oracle measured theirs.

title: A sigil test compiles a live file from another repo, so its subject moves under it and reddens this lane's nightly gate on a defect that does not exist.
detail: Diagnosed by the aeon lane from the source-gate red and verified here. Ruled: a small sigil-owned fixture, never a widened ambient, because widening breaks the next time anyone touches a live game file. Fixture named to aeon; they carve it. Implies a sweep of every read_aeon site naming a game file rather than an engine vocabulary file.

title: Sound-head addresses in seven test files still name the bank they lived in before the re-layout, in the doc comments and the failure messages.
detail: The assertions derive their values and are correct; only the prose is stale. When one of these gates goes red it tells the reader to look a long way from where the bytes are. Verified against the frozen size table.

title: A block body is re-read once for every level of nesting it sits inside, which the reference assembler does not do at all.
detail: Flat in asl, linear here: at depth 32 it is roughly fifty times slower. Near-invisible on the corpus this project benchmarks with (mean nesting depth 0.054) and dominant on the engine (1.157) and on the Sonic 2 disassembly. MEASURE-FIRST: size it on aeon or s2disasm, never on s1disasm.

title: The assembler reads the whole source one more time than the reference does, to prove to itself that nothing changed.
detail: Convergence requires two consecutive identical symbol tables, so the floor is two traversals where asl stops at one, plus one more per forward-referenced equate link. Reached by two seats using different instruments: a pass census forward, marginal-pass calibration in reverse.

title: Rendering one diagnostic walks the source file from the beginning, so an error near the end of a large file is expensive.
detail: Cost depends on both file size and error position, which is what walking from byte zero looks like. Invisible on a corpus with few diagnostics and heavy on one with thousands, and it only bites a FAILING build, which is the build a developer repeats.

title: A masking rule is written out twice in one crate with no shared constant, and the second copy is unreachable.
detail: Its guard flag is constructed nowhere in the repository, verified against a control. The sibling builtin shares a named constant between its two sites; this one does not. If the window ever moves, the live copy is fixed and the dead one is resurrected wrong.

title: A finding deferred in August now costs more than the number everyone is quoting.
detail: Re-derived rather than quoted: the count moved from 53 to 59, six new procs, all engine code written since. The model was validated by reproducing the historical 53 at three separate sweep-era revisions, which is the control that makes the new number credible. The in-code doc and the ledger both state the stale one.

title: The crate split deferred in August is now about seventy percent larger than when it was deferred.
detail: The harness doubled in size and gained a dependency the seam plan predates. Its build-timing half is unmeasurable without a build and those seconds should not be quoted as current.

title: A reviewer's pinned instrument was deleted mid-measurement by another agent sharing the same scratch directory.
detail: Two agents told to write scratch files and not told where are each other's concurrent writer by construction. Every future seat brief names a private scratch directory. The affected seat re-copied, re-verified its digest and re-ran, and retracted the one contaminated number.

title: The Z80 instruction encoder was checked against the reference assembler across hundreds of forms and emits no wrong bytes.
detail: The heaviest measurement in the panel: an independent model transcribed from the encoder, validated against 150 reference-minted vectors, its own harness mutation-checked, then 863 forms swept one reference invocation each with exit status checked. Specifically refuted: no prefixed instruction family silently falls back to its unprefixed form. Recorded as a clean result so a quiet area is not read as an unexamined one.

title: Two reviewers disagreed about whether a linker function is slow, and both were right about different inputs.
detail: ADJUDICATED: P2 measured the AS path, where the whole program is a handful of huge sections and the cost is real; CACHE measured the .emp path, where each module gets its own sections and it is negligible. Neither said which corpus it measured. On the AS path the same function is both quadratic and wrong for one underlying reason, and org exists only there, so one fix addresses both.

title: The Z80 instruction encoder was checked against the reference assembler across hundreds of forms and emits no wrong bytes.
detail: State corrected from decided to holds, the state added to the contract on this row's own first use. The finding is unchanged: an independent model validated against reference-minted vectors, its own harness mutation-checked, then hundreds of forms swept one reference invocation each with exit status checked, and no wrong bytes. Recorded so a quiet area is not read as an unexamined one.

title: Two reviewers disagreed about whether a linker function is slow, and both were right about different inputs.
detail: State corrected from decided to OPEN, NOT to holds. The contract pairs holds with severity clean, a property re-derived and found to hold; this row is severity low and nothing here holds. What was settled is the DISAGREEMENT (two seats measured different corpora and neither said so); the cost itself is real, unfixed, and lives on the AS path where the whole program is a handful of large sections. It is expected to close as a side effect of the correctness parcel now out, since one fix addresses both, and it gets its own fixed line if it does.

detail: Fixed structurally, not by special case: the offset parameter is gone from both lowering seams, which now derive it by sentinel probe, so the wrong-constant class is unrepresentable there. Red-first quoted the wrong bytes; expectations were asl-minted rather than taken from sigil's own AS front end, which carried the same defect and is therefore not an oracle. All four ROMs byte-identical on the merged tree, ROMs deleted first.

The TIE-BREAK was deliberately left alone and reported rather than taken: deciding which run authored a label needs a fragment index on Label, which is front-end territory. The parcel died on the account session limit before its gates; its commit bodies carried the finding and the gates were completed at the landing.

title: Two reviewers disagreed about whether a linker function is slow, and both were right about different inputs.

title: The address-of-here builtin is baked before placement while labels follow placement, so the two disagree.
detail: MEASURED, not reachable today: zero here() call sites across 198 aeon .emp files, comment-stripped scan, control returning 16 hits for a sibling builtin. But it is an ACCIDENT of the corpus, not a design guarantee: every unpinned aeon section satisfies the other conjunct and only seven pinned sections are immune by construction. Severity note: the likeliest first use is a capacity guard, and a here() baked at a module-local zero makes it pass forever, which is worse than a visibly absurd pointer because nothing downstream disagrees. Corrects the brief's mechanism too: code sections are safe because here() cannot appear in code position at all.

detail: frag_start_vma shared the offset-keyed lookup although it is handed a fragment index and never needed one. Its end-to-end ladder case fails on shipped code with wrong CODE: a two-byte branch holding displacement -128 that, at its real site, branches to the wrong address. Now replays the cursor from the rungs directly. Worth recording that the panel did not find this one; the parcel repairing its neighbour did.

title: A sigil test compiles a live file from another repo, so its subject moves under it and reddens this lane's nightly gate on a defect that does not exist.
detail: Fixed at merge 87e8fe11 (commit 9af27c83, carried in on the LS-12 refreeze branch): the two objroutine probes compile a frozen fixture aeon keeps under its own test fixtures, games/sonic4/test/fixtures/sigil_objroutine_probe.emp, whose header records what the probes require of it, and the reference guard names that path so an absent fixture skips by name or fails under SIGIL_STRICT_GATE=1 rather than reading a moving live object. The implied sweep of the remaining read-a-game-file test sites is NOT done and is booked separately as PROBE-GAME-FILE-SWEEP.

title: The sibling the live-game-file finding predicted is in ENGINE source, not game source: a probe compiled a live engine implementation file and doctored one of its literal lines.
detail: Found by the sweep sig-probe-live-game-file booked. broken_falls_into_stub_chain_fires_fallthrough compiled the LIVE engine/objects/collision.emp against a hard-coded five-file ambient and string-doctored 'proc Touch_None () clobbers() falls_into Touch_Enemy {}'. Reproduced: renaming Touch_Enemy to Touch_Badnik in a copy of the reference tree, a refactor with no compiler-behaviour meaning, reds the probe on 'the doctor must have found its target' and prints the whole 58 KB file twice into the failure. Fixed at 898a97b1 by synthesising the stub chain; both arms proven against a mutated lint (lint disabled -> doctored arm reds; lint always-fires -> control arm reds). The deleted live-file control duplicated warn_tier_corpus, which pins proc.undeclared-fallthrough firings per shipped shape across engine/ and games/. The same commit replaced the six-file sources() with reference_tree(['engine/objects/aabb.emp']) so an absent file skips naming the path and fails under SIGIL_STRICT_GATE=1.

title: The engine-vs-game axis the sweep was briefed with is refuted; the axis is content-invariant versus content-snapshot, and sixteen sites pin a snapshot of another repo.
detail: The implied sweep of sig-probe-live-game-file is DONE: 144 of the workspace's 399 test binaries read the aeon tree, and all were read and classified. Measured refutation of the briefed premise that engine vocabulary moves less: since 2026-03-01 engine/system/constants.emp has 79 commits against games/sonic4/config/constants.emp's 37, and engine/objects/collision.emp 24 against engine/objects/sst.emp's 16, so engine files move MORE. The separating property is not the directory but whether an assertion holds for any valid content or pins today's. Sixteen open sites are enumerated by file and line in ledger row PROBE-CONTENT-SNAPSHOT; each is either a deliberate cross-repo tripwire or a coupling whose removal would cost a real non-vacuity control, so none were changed. No new gate: the obvious name-your-reference-paths lint fires on 87 of the 95 aeon_dir callers, an always-red check, and the property worth gating is not decidable from source text.

title: One language's align still writes padding bytes the other language stopped writing two days ago, and the test comparing them cannot see the difference.
detail: Fixed at merge 4f7fc54f: emit_align_pad now calls sigil_ir::asl_align_pad and reserves, where it computed a plain unsigned round-up and emitted a zero Fill. Closed BROADER than the row's where line, which named only the per-item (align: N) path: emit_align_pad is one function with three callers (top-level align N, per-item (align: N), table item_align:), and the DAC's own align is the top-level form, so the row's location was narrower than the defect. THE ROW'S COUPLING CLAIM IS REFUTED, not carried: the DAC intra-bank recompute does not fire because of the Fill and never did. recompute_bank_aligns is guarded by baked_after >= tru while every .emp section chains from the cosmetic base lma_base = 0x0, so the rewrite branch never ran on dac_banks under Fill either; the pad was already correct because lowering origin 0 and a $8000-aligned true base are congruent mod $8000, with the link-time congruence assert backstopping it. The do-not-land-alone warning is retired. Byte differential over all four shapes, both arms, arms proven distinct by assembler md5: no ROM byte moved and the control reconciled with chain tip 205. Two section IMAGES are a byte shorter, which no ROM digest can see; the ripple was two pin lengths and one boundary label, applied by regeneration. Signed-vs-unsigned unified on a measured zero RAM-vma sites, canary-backed. Ledgered separately: LENS-BANK-ALIGN-RECOMPUTE-ORPHANED, since neither front end now produces a zero-Fill pad and two placement functions are dead with respect to their stated subject.

title: A reviewer's pinned instrument was deleted mid-measurement by another agent sharing the same scratch directory.
detail: Closed by making the dispatch practice name a private scratch directory per agent, created before dispatch, stated in the brief as the agent's alone. Banked in the dispatch-practice section and exercised in both briefs dispatched tonight before it was written down. The rule is about construction rather than care: two agents told to build scratch files and not told where to put them are each other's concurrent writer with neither able to detect the other.

title: The address-of-here builtin is baked before placement while labels follow placement, so the two disagree.
detail: CONFIRMED by differential probe, then fixed at 1ae36d3a. Mechanism as the row said, with the route named: a label resolves to vma_base.unwrap_or(lma) + offset, and for a section without an explicit vma: three passes rewrite lma AFTER lowering (resolve::place_sequential on the CLI no-map path, resolve::place_sections under --map, and the linker's place_pass for Chained sections), while here() was baked from the module-local counter. section_has_relaxable answers only whether the OFFSET within the section can move, never whether the BASE is known. Arms PRODUCED on the baseline: a second module's section placed at 0x18 had label Tag = 0x18 and here() = 0x0; a Chained section after a section whose jbra grew had label 206 and here() 204; ensure(here() <= 8) read at module-local 4 passed silently with no link verdict while the placed position was 0x1c. Fix: IrBuilder::position_is_provisional() = (open section's vma_base is None) || section_has_relaxable(), consulted by here_pos and lower_item_guard; the provisional path is the existing D-H machinery (SymRef emit, deferred LinkAssert, [here.provisional] on comptime steering), so emitted and guarded here() become correct and the capacity-guard shape the row feared now FAILS at the placed address. Exact Value::Int kept only where the base is known at lowering: an explicit vma: section with no relaxable before the position. WIDENED REFUSAL, flagged for the owner: a comptime-steering here() in a section without vma: (default text section included) is now [here.provisional], where it baked a module-local integer; no new diagnostic id, message reworded to name both reasons and the vma: remedy. Corpus re-derived: 0 code-position here( across 201 tracked .emp files at aeon ec640bcf (git grep, // comments stripped; 67 raw lines all in comments), control bankid( = 16 under the same filter, so no ROM byte moves. Gate crates/sigil-frontend-emp/tests/here_placement.rs (5 tests, both arms reported, non-vacuity asserted) committed red on 35d24ee2 and proven red again post-fix by restoring builder.rs and lower/mod.rs from 9df49aaf (staged mutation shown by git diff --cached --stat and grep count 0 on disk), then green from 1ae36d3a. The builder.rs comment now states what section_has_relaxable measures and points at position_is_provisional for the base half.

title: The capstone child runner wrote all of the child's stdin before reading any of its stdout, so a suite test could hang instead of failing, and did for 1290 s.
detail: Ledger row CAPSTONE-STREAM-PIPE-DEADLOCK. Fixed at d73c743d: run_piped writes stdin from a joined thread while the caller drains stdout and stderr through wait_with_output; a write error is still an Err, after a failed child status (the old order reported Broken pipe and lost a child's stderr whenever the input exceeded the pipe). Gate sigil-isa/tests/capstone_pipe_discipline.rs: a child that fills its stdout before reading stdin at 2 * fs.pipe-max-size + 1 bytes each way, under a 120 s watchdog; proven red-first by re-applying write-then-read to the fixed runner (0 passed, 4 failed, 120 s to the watchdog) and restoring from the committed bytes. Measured against the row: the corpus at aeon ec640bcf is 3257 byte strings = 94,453 bytes of stdin, not 325,830; the child answers 1.6x; with a default 64 KiB pipe and python 3.14's 128 KiB stdout buffer the old order completes to 145,000 bytes and deadlocks from 174,000, so the real corpus cannot deadlock on a default pipe; at one-page pipes (what the kernel hands a user past fs.pipe-user-pages-soft, which a full-suite run's child pipes can exceed) the real corpus deadlocks every time. The hanging run's pipe size was not witnessed. Enumerated every write-to-child-stdin site in the repo (Rust Command/Stdio/.stdin(/wait_with_output/child.stdin; python subprocess/Popen/communicate/input=; shell scripts): the only one is this runner.

title: A generated field the manifest calls dead is still stamped into hundreds of lines, and names test binaries that do not exist.
detail: Fixed at 53bc85de. The tests field is deleted from the manifest AND from the grammar: RomSpec, RegionSpec, SymbolSpec and OffsetSpec all carry serde(deny_unknown_fields), so with the field gone a row that spells one is a PARSE ERROR rather than a silently ignored line, which is what makes the deletion durable instead of cosmetic. pins.rs was REGENERATED by the tool, never hand-edited. THE COUNT WAS 512, NOT THE 412 THE HEADER AND THE LEDGER ROW BOTH CLAIMED. Instrument: /usr/bin/grep -c '^tests = [' on the manifest; corroborated by git grep -c (512), by the 512 tests: doc suffixes in the committed pins.rs, and by repin's own drift report printing 512 committed-only and 512 regenerated-only lines. No array spanned two lines. 412 was never right at the commit that wrote it: 22b1a19f and its parent both measure 512; walking the file history, 412 was the early-August 2026 figure, carried forward unchanged while the real one climbed past 510. Corrected in place in docs/OVERSEER.md and docs/OVERSEER-ROW-HISTORY.md, where the figure is, not appended below it. NO PIN VALUE MOVED, proven. Control first: repin --check against the reference tree exited 0 on the committed pins.rs before any edit, so the whole-file baseline was established rather than assumed. After: all 523 pub const declarations extracted and sorted from both files are byte-identical (md5 fe3a4dd7ae97af56e23c94b219fe4026 each), diff empty, and a negative control changing one hex digit is visible to that same instrument. Gate: repin::tests::a_tests_field_is_a_manifest_parse_error, proven red by putting the field back on RegionSpec and SymbolSpec (mutation shown on disk by grep and by git diff --stat before the red run) and restored from the committed baseline. Verified with SIGIL_STRICT_GATE=1 and AEON_DIR at aeon ec640bcf: 226 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored across --lib, repin_pins, repin_gate_message and region_end_contracts; clippy --release --workspace --all-targets -D warnings exits 0, with a planted needless_range_loop in a sigil-cli test target making the same command exit 101 as the coverage control.

title: A number of pinned regions have no consumer anywhere in the code.
detail: Fixed at 53bc85de by REPORTING the set, not by deleting anything. repin now prints the zero-consumer pins by NAME on every run, before the unchanged-early-return, GATED BY NOTHING, on this repo's own PROVENANCE-REV-REACHABILITY precedent: a declared exception list is a population to maintain whose failure mode is going green because nobody maintained it. NEITHER EARLIER COUNT SURVIVED RE-DERIVATION. Seat GATE said 33, seat B2b said 22; the set at 53bc85de has 21 members: ABILITY_NONE,DUST_ANIMS DUST_DATA,DUST_PUFF EPILOGUE,KNUCKLES KNUCKLES_ANIMS,KNUCKLES_DATA OBJCODEBASE,OBJECT_TEST_STATE PAGE_CACHE_ALLOC_FRAME,PAGE_CACHE_PUBLISH PAGE_IN_FLUSH,PAL_SONIC_TAILS PARALLAX_STATE,PLAYER_FLY REPLAY_FIXTURE,SEC_LEN TAILS_ANIMS,TAILS_DATA TEST_ENEMY_INIT. PREDICATE, stated in the report's own output: no .rs file outside src/pins.rs contains the constant's name as a whole identifier token. Token and not substring, and the difference is real: under a substring predicate one member drops off because a longer identifier in a comment ends in its name. Derived twice by independent instruments that agree exactly: git ls-files '*.rs' minus pins.rs, tokenized and comm'd against the pub const names, and the tool's own on-disk walk of crates/ excluding target dirs. THE DELETE-THEM FIX IS WRONG AND THE MECHANISM WAS CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED: drift_report compares strip_provenance(committed) to strip_provenance(generated) over the WHOLE text and pins_rs_is_current panics on any Some, so an unconsumed pin whose engine symbol moves still turns that gate red. Deleting the orphans would remove drift coverage of every symbol deleted. The report says so in its own output. WRITING ABOUT A PIN CONSUMES IT: the first draft of the predicate's doc comment named a real constant as its example, and the sweep read that comment as a reference and dropped that pin from its own list, 20 names instead of 21. The doc comment now states the shape, never a name, and says why. The block is emitted ONLY by src/bin/repin.rs, never from DriftReport's Display and never from stale_pins_message, because the aeon lane's tools/freeze_preflight.sh greps that failure text to tell a stale instrument from a real cross-seam defect. Verified firsthand that tests/repin_pins.rs uses the library and never spawns the binary, so the tool's stdout is invisible to that test. Three tests, each proven red with the mutation shown applied and restored from the committed baseline: the token predicate (mutated to substring), the block's two forbidden grammars (a test-FAILED line and the stale-listings string, proven in separate runs because the first assert short-circuits the second), and the boundary itself (the block spliced into stale_pins_message).

title: The engine-vs-game axis the sweep was briefed with is refuted; the axis is content-invariant versus content-snapshot, and sixteen sites pin a snapshot of another repo.
detail: DECIDED by the sigil overseer 2026-09-09 under the standing grant on assembler internals, and recorded rather than filed as a card because the reason it would be the owner's is not one this seat can state: no ROM byte, no language surface, no cost to him either way. NO LINT IS BUILT. Grounds, measured rather than argued: the obvious rule, that a reference-dependent test must name its paths through reference_tree(...), fires on 87 of the 95 files calling aeon_dir, and a check that is red on correct code trains people to weaken it, which is this lane's banked always-red rule. The property actually worth gating, that a probe must not pin a snapshot of foreign content, is NOT decidable from source text: assert_eq!(sites, 6) and assert_eq!(walked_debug_shapes, 3) are the same syntax and only one is over another repo's content. A declared register of exceptions was also refused, on this lane's own precedent twice over, because its failure mode is going green when nobody maintains it. What stands instead of a gate: the sixteen sites are enumerated by full path in the ledger row, and on 2026-09-08 they were ROUTED to the aeon lane with the path rather than a summary, so the only lane whose edits can trip them now has a live reader and has confirmed two of its in-flight parcels land on them. SET ASIDE, not fixed: the exposure is unchanged and is written down. Re-open if a red from one of these sites ever costs more than the enumeration saves.

The forced-top closure was already computed for the dead-save consumer, so the added work is one check_firings call and both lists come from the SAME analysis the build gate runs. NOTHING GATES ON THE NUMBER, deliberately: a test asserting 59 rots exactly as the prose did and goes red on correct code the day the sixtieth contract lands. Measured against the reference tree (aeon ec640bcf) at de5327c0: sonic4 plain 11 sites, 0 firings trusting, 59 forced, COST 59; --debug 60; --game demo 58. The 59 independently reproduces the 2026-09-06 sweep's re-derivation, which recorded no command. All four now name the command; the two dated review documents keep their figure with its measurement date beside the command. A NEIGHBOURING FIGURE WITH THE SAME ROT, found in the same comment and swept with it: closure.rs and the ledger row both said aeon carries 8 such sites, and the ledger row then listed ten files. The report counts 11 for the plain shape and a source grep counts 12; the one it cannot see is collision.emp:78's TouchHandler dispatch, inside a splice the corpus walk does not resolve, which is the sub-finding the 2026-09-06 sweep moved from latent to live. detail: FIXED as a quoting defect only; THE DEFERRAL ITSELF STAYS OPEN and still wants the owner session on the seam choices. The LOC half is now derivable: scripts/s8_seam_size.sh holds the seam table the ledger row names, prints per-seam and total counts, states what it counted (physical lines of crates/sigil-harness/src/<module>.rs), and separately names the modules the seam plan does NOT claim, which is the part of the crate the plan has no home for and which prose cannot keep current. It reports and does not gate; it exits 2 only when a named module has moved out from under the table. RED-FIRST for that loud path: renaming `provenance` to `provenance_RENAMED` in the seam table (mutation quoted from disk and shown by git diff --stat) made it exit 2 with a MISSING line, and the silently wrong total it would otherwise have printed was 16195 rather than 18257; restored with git checkout de5327c0 -- scripts/s8_seam_size.sh (which stages, so cleanliness was checked with git status) and re-ran green at exit 0. It is wired into NO runner, deliberately: the only nightly runner in this repo is a gate runner, and an always-moving number does not belong in one. MY COUNT DISAGREES WITH THE SWEEP'S and I did not reconcile it: the 2026-09-06 sweep put the move at ~15,800, the script says 18257 at a later master. The sweep recorded no basis for its figure, which is the whole reason the command now exists; the script's basis is stated in the script. FIVE SITES carried the S8 figures, two more than the brief's starting set: docs/reviews/2026-08-14-lens-sweep-closeout.md:34, campaign-gap-ledger.md:2332, the origin packet docs/reviews/2026-08-13-sigil-lens-sweep.md at its S8 section and again in its priority list, and the ledger's carried-forward line at :4358.

title: The extra traversal is the bonus pass after convergence, not the convergence rule, and on the corpus roots it exists only because the build fails.
detail: MEASURED, not fixed; severity lowered from medium. Note: docs/superpowers/notes/2026-09-08-extra-traversal-measure.md. The exit condition is `pass > 0 && env == prev`, floor 2, CONFIRMED. Refuted: asl does NOT stop at 1 (it takes 2 passes on s1disasm, on s2disasm and on any forward-referencing source; 1 pass only with no forward reference at all), and asl does NOT resolve a forward equ chain in 2 (it refuses it, error #1010, twice, non-zero exit, where sigil resolves it correctly). The extra traversal is NOT the convergence loop: it converges at the floor on s1disasm and on all seven shipped aeon shapes. It is the BONUS PASS AFTER convergence, `force_relocate` on aeon and `poison` on the corpora. Counts: aeon all shapes 3 (2 convergence + 1 force_relocate bonus); s1disasm sigil 3 vs asl 2, 50 errors; s2disasm sigil 5 vs asl 2, 5151 errors. PER TRAVERSAL sigil is 1.24x asl on s1disasm and 1.13x on s2disasm against an output-free asl (1.05x/1.03x against asl also writing listing and object), so the whole deficit is COUNT. Marginal cost fitted over 5 chain lengths: 0.2852 s per traversal, intercept -0.03 s, corroborating P1b's 0.246 s. PRICED: folding the force_relocate bonus saves 0.021 s per aeon build, 4.8% of a whole demo build, and is the ONLY saving on the shipping path; folding the poison bonus saves 33% on s1disasm and 20% on s2disasm but only on FAILING builds; chasing equ chains in-pass saves 2.0 s on a synthetic k=8 probe and zero on everything this project builds; an asl-style 1-pass exit saves zero everywhere. CONFOUND CHECKED: the conclusion holds (understated) but the mechanism is wrong, the CLI route DOES run resolve_layout and link (main.rs:141,150); the corpus runs exit 1 at main.rs:124 because they FAIL. asl's listing plus object is 16% of its s1disasm time and 9% of its s2disasm time. Both halves of the 2x are artifacts of one thing, sigil not yet assembling those trees. Left actionable only as the force_relocate bonus pass; reopen if the owner wants 0.021 s per build chased.
